messages:
sam: Heads-up — pushed a tiny kernel-routing change to prefer fused-attn for batch sizes <= 8. Perf job shows a 12% regression on long-seq paged-attn runs when KV paging is active. Repro steps and traces below.

maria: oof. did the change alter prefetch behavior or allocator hints?

sam: quick summary: before change we used flashv2 for small batches and fused-attn only when seq<=512 and KV cache resident. change switched selection to fused-attn earlier to reduce kernel-switch overhead. CI microbench (no paging) looked neutral. But paged workload with frequent KV churn regressed.

alex: can you paste the perf numbers?

sam: sure — microbench vs paged test:
```
baseline (flashv2-prefetch=true): throughput=310 tokens/s, p99=24ms
new (fused-prefersmall=true): throughput=273 tokens/s, p99=31ms
delta: -12% throughput, +29% p99
```
Also seeing increased GPU memcpy stalls in the flamegraph when we hit a KV page-in.

jon: flamegraph snippet?

sam: pasted flamegraph stack (trimmed):
```
rpc_recv -> scheduler -> kernel_chooser(fused) -> fused_attn_launch -> kv_page_in -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> sync -> wait_for_io
```
Note: when fused_attn is chosen, we end up doing an extra small host->device memcpy for KV page paths because fused kernel expects a packed layout and we do a transient pack. flashv2 path has an alternate packing path that can stream from pinned buffer without the intermediate copy.

maria: so fused-attn adds an extra memcpy on KV page miss + packing? that explains stalls. any idea why CI microbench missed it?

sam: microbench doesn't exercise KV paging or async page-in races — it's mostly resident-cache runs. Regression only visible on paged-attn with eviction churn.

alex: is this the packing behavior we observed in the paged-attn RFC? we had two choices: in-kernel reformat vs prepack. Looks like fused required prepack in userland for now.

sam: correct. fused_attn current impl uses host-side packing for better arithmetic throughput, but that creates an extra memcpy on page-in. flashv2 uses a kernel-friendly pinned scatter path that overlaps IO+repack better.

jon: can we short-circuit fused path when page-in latency > X ms? i.e., kernel policy: if recent_page_miss_rate > 0.1 then prefer flashv2.

sam: proposal: revert the routing change and instead add an allocator hint + prefetch tweak: set slot_reserve=2 for hot prefixes, and enable prefault_on_hotprefix for the pager. That reduces page-in frequency and keeps fused benefits for true in-cache cases.

maria: timeline? we need a hotfix for customer-facing clusters.

sam: I can push a rollback of chooser by EOD. Meanwhile I pushed an experiment branch with allocator hint:
```
pager_config {
  prefetch_policy: "prefault_on_hotprefix"
  hotprefix_reserve: 2
}
```
Initial run shows throughput back to 305 tokens/s and p99 26ms.

alex: good. can we add a telemetry flag to emit recent_page_miss_rate per model-route (low-overhead counter) so chooser can make smarter decisions?

jon: also add a metric for memcpy_wait_time to see how much time is spent in the transient pack path.

sam: will add both: metrics 'model.kv.page_miss_rate' and 'model.kv.pack_memcpy_ms'. will gate higher-cardinality on dedicated customers.

infra-bot: deploy started: roll back chooser-reroute-4412345678 -> roll back fused-pref-policy (canary 2/5 nodes).

maria: once rollback lands, let's run the KV-thrash litmus with the allocator hint branch. I want numbers across seq lens {512,1024,2048} and batch sizes {1,4,8}.

sam: logging the test matrix. early results:
- seq512 batch4: baseline 320 -> new 318 (ok)
- seq1024 batch4: baseline 290 -> new 286 (ok)
- seq2048 batch4: baseline 260 -> new 252 (regression without prefetch), with prefetch: 258
- batch1/8 combos show fused helps when prefetch reduces miss rate < 3%

alex: caution: increasing hotprefix_reserve increases memory pressure on block table — watch allocator fragmentation. any compaction changes?

sam: noted. allocator stat snapshot:
```
block_table_slots: 131072
used_slots: 98432
fragmentation_pct: 12.4
hot_reserve_allocated: 256
```
with hotprefix_reserve=2 we allocate ~0.2% more slots in steady state. fragmentation ticked +0.7% in stress test.

maria: that seems acceptable short-term. long-term we should make hot-reserve an LRU-backed hint so it doesn't permanently bloat.

jon: agree. also consider an adaptive chooser: if pack_memcpy_ms / kernel_exec_ms > 0.2 then prefer flashv2 for the next N requests. Lightweight and reactive.

sam: I'll prototype chooser cooldown using EWMA of pack_memcpy_ratio. if ratio > 0.15 -> bias towards flashv2 for 500ms.

alex: can we add a forced debug flag to the runtime to always simulate a 2ms memcpy on page-in so we can test heuristics in CI?

sam: good idea. add env RUNTIME_SIM_PACK_COPY_MS=2. will add to perf harness.

maria: next steps:
1) roll back chooser change (inflight)
2) deploy allocator-hint branch to canary with prefault_on_hotprefix
3) land telemetry and dbg env var for CI
4) prototype EWMA chooser cooldown

jon: +1. thanks for catching this quickly.

sam: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short PR that documents the packing tradeoffs and the safety fallback in chooser.

alex: please attach the perf harness command you used so we can reproduce.

sam: harness command:
```
./perf_harness --model paged-attn-bert --seq 2048 --batch 4 --kv-evict-rate 0.12 --runtime-sim-pack-copy-ms ${RUNTIME_SIM_PACK_COPY_MS:-0}
```
I'll drop raw logs in the bench run artifact.

infra-bot: rollback canary completed: 2/2 nodes reverted.

maria: good. after we get stable numbers let's close the RFC loop on pack-vs-prepack options for fused. Prefer an implementation where fused can accept streamed pinned buffers to avoid extra memcpy on page-in.

sam: agreed — long-term fix is fused kernel variant that supports streaming input layout. short-term: chooser + prefetch + telemetry.

jon: lgtm.

sam: closing out — will open PRs and tag infra for canary rollout plan. :thumbsup:
